newsitem.title: UK: Short bunker fuel deliveries could cost $90 mln.
newsitem.headline: Short bunker fuel deliveries could cost $90 mln.

text.p: More than 20 percent of all bunker fuels deliveries were significantly short in quantity last year, a report said on Tuesday.

The report produced for the Oslo-based tanker organisation Intertanko said "grey margins" -- the difference between what is ordered by a shipping company and what is delivered by a supplier -- totalled $78 million in 1996.
It said that if bunker prices remained at current levels of about $125 a tonne, this could rise to $90 million this year.
Mikal Boe of CBC Marine Publications, the London company which compiled the report, said: "It is actually equivalent to a loss of around 50 cents on every single tonne of bunkers bought.
"The losses are staggering, and it's hard to see how some of the suppliers get away with it. Shipowners should look into this, because there are massive savings to be made here."
"One way in which shipowners can virtually eliminate short deliveries is simply to deal only with the suppliers in these ports which have a track record of not short delivering their customers."
The report named 14 ports which this month stand out because of their higher-than-normal quantity risk. They include Rotterdam, Fujairah, Singapore and San Francisco.
A tanker bunker manager said the report did not surprise him. "It's well known that owners are cheated on quantity but it's very difficult to pinpoint."
"We are always exposed (to some risk) but we avoid suppliers with a bad reputation," added the manager, who asked not to be named.

Intertanko comprises 250 tanker owners and represents nearly 80 percent of the world independent tanker fleet. It publishes the so-called "White List," a regular report on quantity risk from bunker suppliers. -- London newsroom +44 542 171 4088
